Method of Attack: Acts as a backdoor providing access when other mechanisms fail or are removed
Uses multiple vulnerable WordPress websites for command and control (C2) and hosting malicious PowerShell scripts
Exfiltrates sensitive data including master passwords for password management software using malicious PowerShell scripts
Commands executed via compromised websites include timeout, changeshell, changepoint, get, post, killme
Data exfiltration through recursive file enumeration and archiving, excluding .MP4 files
Discoverer: Cisco Talos security researchers in collaboration with CERT.NGO
Impacted Systems: Organizations in various sectors including government, military, education, research, pharmaceutical, NGOs
Attack Vector: Compromise of legitimate but vulnerable WordPress websites used as C2 servers
Delivery of malicious PowerShell scripts via compromised WordPress sites
Indicators of Compromise: Small set of indicators of compromise for TinyTurla-NG available in .TXT and .JSON format from Cisco Talos
